note: Frozen check list for technical-writing evals 1-6. Written before any run of these evals and not to be edited to fit an output. Its author had read the skill, evals.json, the fixtures and the note on this skill in MAINTAINING.md, which describes in a few lines three smoke sessions of 2026-11-22 whose outputs were not kept (eval 1 with and without the skill, eval 3 with it): no output was read, but checks 1.4, 3.20 and 3.21 touch things that note mentions (a section added without the skill; a management UI and a usual cause stated with it). Each assertion in evals.json is decomposed into atomic yes/no checks. kind=file and kind=absence are decided by a script from the bytes on disk after the run; in eval 5, which has no fixture, the only file is the reply, and check 5.2 is decided on the tool calls the session recorded. kind=reply, kind=invention and kind=negative are decided by an LLM judge. A met kind=reply check quotes the words or the file:line that satisfy it. kind=invention and kind=negative are negatives: when met there is nothing to quote and the evidence is the search; when unmet the offending words are quoted. 'A passive without an agent' means a passive verb whose sentence does not say who or what performs the action; a verb that describes a state ('is written in Go') is not one. In eval 3 the expected output accepts questions asked before writing: checks 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.8 and 3.9 describe the runbook and are not met in a run that wrote no runbook, the negatives of that eval are then decided on the reply, and the iteration reports such a run apart, with the totals given both ways. In evals 2 and 3 the document may be written at any path: the judge decides on the file the run created, and on the reply when it created none. A fact that must be present is one check per fact. A borderline case resolves to not met. More text never raises a verdict.
